failure_modes.recovery: Call workflow_list to find a valid id.
failure_modes.when: the id does not exist in your tenant

failure_modes.recovery: Re-read the workflow, merge, retry with the fresh updated_at.
failure_modes.when: expected_updated_at was passed and another writer changed the row first

failure_modes.recovery: Remove the {{credential:...}} reference, or ask an owner or admin to make this change. Renaming or switching it on or off needs no admin.
failure_modes.when: the change touches the steps or trigger of a workflow that uses a saved credential ({{credential:...}}) and the caller's role is below admin (reason SIMPLER_WORKFLOW_CREDENTIAL_SAVE_NEEDS_ADMIN)

failure_modes.recovery: Save the same change with is_active 0 and ask a person to switch it on in Workflows. Nothing was changed.
failure_modes.when: an agent token would leave a schedule or webhook workflow switched on that runs, before or after this save, as a person whose role or access the token does not fully hold (reason SIMPLER_WORKFLOW_ARM_NEEDS_PERSON); a steps or trigger change makes the token's own person the one it runs as

preconditions: id is required. next_run_at is server-computed — any value you send is ignored.

A change to the steps or trigger, by a person or by their agent token, makes that person the one its scheduled and webhook runs act as, at their own role; the answer's runs_as says so. Renaming or switching it on or off keeps its author: switching on a schedule or webhook workflow someone else last changed answers runs_as with that person's name and role, or with both null when they are no longer a member and its runs will not start.

description: Edit a workflow's fields or its definition graph: every call re-validates the definition — yours if resent, else the stored one decoded back — against the resulting trigger_type, so a plain rename can fail if that stored graph no longer validates, and flipping to 'schedule' without a schedule block fails here rather than at the scheduler. When trigger_type ends as 'schedule' and is_active as 1, next_run_at recomputes from schedule and now on every call, even one touching neither field; any value you send for it is ignored. Optional expected_updated_at compare-and-set: a stale value refuses CONFLICT — re-read, merge, retry. NEXT: workflow_read to confirm the new next_run_at.

expected_updated_at.description: Optional compare-and-set guard: the updated_at from a prior workflow_read/workflow_list. Mismatch returns CONFLICT with the current value.

name: workflow_update
